value.body: A B.Voc trains you in a specific trade, so some graduates start a small enterprise or freelance in it — a service unit, workshop, salon, food business, repair or IT services. Government schemes offer collateral-free loans and capital subsidies for new micro units.

items.label: PMMY (Mudra) loans
items.note: Shishu up to ₹50,000; Kishore to ₹5 lakh; Tarun to ₹10 lakh; Tarun Plus to ₹20 lakh for past Tarun borrowers

items.label: PMEGP project cost
items.note: Subsidy 15–35% depending on category and area

items.label: Udyam registration
items.note: MSME registration used for many schemes

value.title: How you get in
value.body: No exam. You need a business plan, any trade licences your work needs, and usually some own funds (PMEGP asks for a 5–10% own contribution). Loans are applied for through banks, and PMEGP through its online portal; a bank still appraises the project.

value.title: At a glance
items: A loan must be repaid even if the business struggles, so early cash flow matters.
Many people work for an employer first to learn the trade and build a client base.
Income is irregular at first; GST and local licences apply once you cross thresholds or by type of trade.
